title: Small etale set-sheaf sections extend to a big ph sheaf
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes and admissible small site presentations as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Use small etale sites and the inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions of sheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $F$ be any sheaf of sets on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$. On the category of schemes over $T$, define $H_F$ by
$$H_F(b:W\to T)=\Gamma(W_{\mathrm{et}},b^{-1}F).$$
For a morphism $c:W'\to W$ over $T$, its restriction map sends a section $s$ to its inverse-image section $c^{-1}s$, using the canonical composition identification $c^{-1}b^{-1}F\simeq(bc)^{-1}F$. Then $H_F$ is a sheaf for the big ph topology [def-trf-ph-scheme-site], the topology generated by Zariski covering families and singleton proper surjections. No abelian-group structure, torsion, constructibility, Noetherianity or finite-presentation assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 0DDW (lemma-describe-pullback-pi-ph), the sheaf assertion for arbitrary sheaves of sets, with the inverse-image restriction maps of the preceding setup.

proof.text: The unit-compatible composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] give $(cd)^*s=d^*(c^*s)$ after the specified identifications; the identity unit acts as the identity by the adjunction identity. Hence the displayed rule defines a presheaf. For $b:W\to T$ put $G=b^{-1}F$. An open immersion $j:O\hookrightarrow W$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-restriction], $j^{-1}G$ is the restriction of $G$ and its unit pulls a section back by ordinary restriction. Combining this with the composition-unit formula identifies $H_F(O)$ and all its open restriction maps with $G(O)$. The sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] for $G$ on the small etale site therefore proves Zariski gluing for $H_F$, including the empty covering of the empty scheme.

source.place: Tag 0DDW (lemma-describe-pullback-pi-ph), first proof paragraph; Tag 09XN (lemma-describe-pullback), Zariski case of the section formula.

proof.text: Fix any proper surjection $p:V\to W$ over $T$ and keep $G=b^{-1}F$. Put $Q=V\times_WV$, with projections $r_i$ and $q=pr_i$, using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $A=p_*p^{-1}G$ and $B=q_*q^{-1}G$. For $i=1,2$ let $\alpha_i:A\to B$ be $p_*$ of the unit for $r_i$, followed by the composition comparisons; direct-image evaluation is $(p_*K)(U)=K(U\times_WV)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. The unit $\eta:G\to A$ equalizes them, because both composites are the unit for $q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] the sheaf equalizer $E$ exists and is computed as $E(U)=\{z\in A(U):\alpha_1z=\alpha_2z\}$. Write $\theta:G\to E$ for the unit factorization. We will prove $\theta$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0DDW (lemma-describe-pullback-pi-ph), reduction to an equalizer of sheaves.

proof.text: Each $r_i$ is a base change of $p$, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]; $q=pr_1$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. For a geometric point $s:P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to W$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, put $V_s=V\times_WP$, $a:V_s\to P$, and $Q_s=Q\times_WP$. Fibre-product universality [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $Q_s=V_s\times_PV_s$, its projections $\rho_i$, and its structure map $d=a\rho_i$. The base-change lemmas make $a$ proper and surjective, so $V_s$ is nonempty and, by [def-weil-proper-morphism], of finite type over $\Omega$. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] it has a closed point $v$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)\to P$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse followed by the point map gives $e:P\to V_s$ with $ae=1_P$. This section exists only on the geometric fibre; we do not claim a section of $p$.

source.place: Tag 0DDW, geometric-fibre reduction; morphisms.tex Tags 01W4, 01W3, 01S1; varieties.tex Tag 0478 and morphisms.tex Tag 01TB.

proof.text: Put $L=s^{-1}G$. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-proper-set-sheaf-base-change] to $p$ with sheaf $p^{-1}G$ and to $q$ with sheaf $q^{-1}G$, along $s$. The morphisms are proper by step 3 and all objects are schemes, so both applications have exactly their required hypotheses. Using inverse-image composition [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] and taking sections over $P$ gives $\Gamma(P,s^{-1}A)\cong\Gamma(V_s,a^{-1}L)$ and $\Gamma(P,s^{-1}B)\cong\Gamma(Q_s,d^{-1}L)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-sections-stalk-natural] these identify $A_s$ and $B_s$ with the indicated fibre sections, and $G_s$ with $\Gamma(P,L)$. All these are bijections of sets, with no group structure or torsion requirement.

source.place: Tag 0DDW, stalk calculation, using Tag 0A3U (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star), equivalently Tag 0A3T; geometric-point sections as in Tag 03Q1.

proof.text: We check the arrows in these identifications. For $f:Z\to W$ and its fibre square with $s$, write $j:Z_s\to Z$ and $\beta:s^{-1}f_*K\to f_{s,*}j^{-1}K$ for the counit mate of [lem-sfb-scheme-proper-set-sheaf-base-change]. Transposing its defining counit composite and cancelling $\epsilon_f f^{-1}\circ f^{-1}\eta_f=1$ gives $s_*\beta\circ\eta_{s,f_*K}=f_*\eta_{j,K}$ under $s_*f_{s,*}=f_*j_*$. Thus on a germ represented by $z\in K(Z\times_WU)$ at a pointed neighbourhood $(U,u)$, the fibre-section map pulls $z$ back along $(\operatorname{pr}_Z,u\operatorname{pr}_P):Z_s\to Z\times_WU$. The representative formula of [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-sections-stalk-natural] gives exactly this germ. Applying this to $p,q$, a representative of $\alpha_i z$ is the pullback of $z$ along $Q\times_WU\to V\times_WU$. Restricting it to $Q_s$ is the same as first restricting $z$ to $V_s$ then pulling back along $\rho_i$: the two maps to $V\times_WU$ have the same projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. For a germ of $G$ both composites pull its representative back to $V_s$. The unit-composition formula [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] therefore identifies $\eta_s$ with $a^*$ and $(\alpha_i)_s$ with $\rho_i^*$.

source.place: Tag 0DDW, sentence identifying the two arrows with projection pullbacks; Tag 0A3U, canonical mate, and Tag 03Q1, germ formula.

proof.text: If $z\in\Gamma(V_s,a^{-1}L)$ equalizes $\rho_1^*,\rho_2^*$, pull that equality back along $h=(1_{V_s},ea):V_s\to V_s\times_PV_s$. By [def-pc-fibre-product] its composites are $\rho_1h=1$ and $\rho_2h=ea$. Hence $z=a^*(e^*z)$ by the unit-composition formula [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. Conversely $a^*t$ equalizes because $a\rho_1=a\rho_2$, and $e^*a^*t=t$ because $ae=1$. This proves the fibre equalizer bijection with inverse $z\mapsto e^*z$. It works for every sheaf $L$, including when its section set is empty; connectedness or reducedness of $V_s$ is unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 0DDW, last paragraph: explicit contraction of the geometric-fibre equalizer using the point from step 3.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-stalk-finite-limits], $E_s$ is the equalizer of $(\alpha_i)_s$. Steps 4--6 show that $\theta_s:G_s\to E_s$ is bijective. Choose a geometric point above each point of $W$; [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks] makes $\theta$ an isomorphism. For empty $W$ the same criterion uses the empty family, so no geometric fibre has to be chosen. Evaluating the equalizer at $W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] now proves that $\Gamma(W,G)\to\Gamma(V,p^{-1}G)\rightrightarrows\Gamma(Q,q^{-1}G)$ is an equalizer with the specified projection pullbacks. By the composition formula [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], these are exactly $H_F(W),H_F(V),H_F(Q)$ and their restriction maps. Thus $H_F$ has unique descent for every singleton proper surjection over $T$.

source.place: Tag 0DDW, passage from stalk equalizers to sheaves and then to global sections; Tags 03PT and 03PU, set-valued forms; Sites Tag 00W2.

proof.text: We finish the topology argument explicitly, rather than assuming descent for the generators suffices without base changes. Let $\{W_i\to W\}$ be any ph covering family. Its generated sieve pulls back to a covering sieve on every affine open $A\subset W$ by [def-trf-ph-scheme-site, def-weil-pbc-topos]. By [lem-trf-ph-affine-standard-sieve-basis], it contains a standard family $V_k\to V\xrightarrow{p}A$, where $p$ is proper surjective and the finitely many $V_k$ form an affine open cover of $V$, each composite factoring through some $W_i$. If two sections of $H_F(W)$ agree on all $W_i$, they agree on $V_k$, hence on $V$ by step 1, and on $A$ by the injectivity in step 7. An affine open cover exists by [lem-pc-fppf-affine-open-cover], so step 1 makes them equal on $W$. This proves separatedness for every ph covering family, including every base change of the given family.

source.place: Topologies Tag 0DBQ (lemma-characterize-sheaf), proof, uniqueness and affine reduction; basis from Tag 0DBL.

proof.text: First suppose $W=A$ affine and let $s_i\in H_F(W_i)$ be a matching family. Choose the standard refinement from step 8, with a chosen factorization for each $V_k$. Pull back the corresponding $s_i$ to $V_k$. They agree on $V_k\cap V_l$, since both maps to the original covering members give a map to their overlap by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Step 1 glues them to $z\in H_F(V)$. The two pullbacks of $z$ to $V\times_AV$ agree: on the Zariski covering by $V_k\times_AV_l$ they are restrictions of the two original matching sections. Step 1 detects their equality there. Step 7 therefore gives a unique $t_A\in H_F(A)$ pulling back to $z$. For each $i$, its pullback and $s_i$ agree on every $V_k\times_AW_i$, by the original matching condition and the defining property of $z$. This is a ph covering of $W_i$: the standard refinement is covering by [lem-trf-ph-affine-standard-sieve-basis] and covering sieves are stable under pullback [def-weil-pbc-topos]. Step 8 then gives equality on $W_i$. Thus $t_A$ amalgamates the whole original family, not just the refinement.

source.place: Tag 0DBQ (lemma-characterize-sheaf), proof, standard-cover gluing and verification on the original covering.

proof.text: For general $W$, choose an affine open covering $\{A_j\}$ by [lem-pc-fppf-affine-open-cover]. Apply step 9 to the ph covering $\{W_i\times_WA_j\to A_j\}$ and the restricted matching family, obtaining $t_j$. On $A_j\cap A_l$, their restrictions agree after the covering pulled back from $\{W_i\to W\}$, as both restrict to the given $s_i$. Step 8 proves that they agree on the intersection, without requiring that intersection to be affine. Step 1 glues the $t_j$ to $t\in H_F(W)$. On each $W_i$, $t$ and $s_i$ agree on its open cover $\{W_i\times_WA_j\}$, hence agree by step 1. Uniqueness is step 8. Every refinement and fibre product used stays in [def-weil-size-convention]; the basis node explicitly includes empty affine targets and empty covers. This proves the ph sheaf axiom for the original presheaf and its specified restriction maps, for arbitrary $F$. Finally apply the family assertion to the small family of all arrows of any covering sieve. Its compatibility is exactly a matching family on that sieve, so existence and uniqueness are the sieve sheaf axiom of [def-weil-pbc-topos].

source.place: Tag 0DBQ (lemma-characterize-sheaf), proof, final local-to-global gluing and omitted overlap verification, written out.
